The guest states are hit too, even though b.css:259-268 sets -webkit-line-clamp:none / overflow:visible on phone/desk/day/print with the comment 'Only the owner's rows, which open, may trim'. The JS overrides that CSS intent at large text: at a 24px root the received DESK renders all seven titles as one word each, phone at 390 renders 'Menu tasting at...' and 'Choose the evening...', and print trims too. That is the screen the whole company is judged by, and interaction-check.mjs:2199 cannot see it because it runs at the default root. The proposed fix is correct for the owner states and does not cost the two-line clamp: driving the line-box predicate over the real DOM, owner-flight stays untrimmed at roots 16-34, and a genuinely long title still clamps to exactly two lines at 390/768/1440 at both 16 and 24 - measurably BETTER than today, where the same long title at a 24px root collapses to 'A...' at 1440 and 'A very long name...' at 390. over() is called only from clamp() (verified: render-core.js:212 and :214 are its only callers), so nothing else moves, and the gates stay green because nothing trims differently at a 16px root.
